content:
maya: Heads up — after the 23:00 rollout to eu1 we saw a short-lived p95 spike (~600ms -> 1.2s) on the tinyprobe healthcheck for embed routes. Not persistent but repeating for ~3 minutes.
deploy-bot: Deploy finished: roll 2026.03.21-rc3 -> eu1. Canary passed initial checks. No automatic rollback triggered. :white_check_mark:
maya: Attaching the tinyprobe output, it's the small synthetic that hits /v1/embed with 16 token inputs.
ops-bot: Alert: tinyprobe-eu1 latency anomaly detected (p95 > 1s) 3 occurrences. Severity: low.
lina: Can you paste the probe snippet and the exact timestamps? I'll pull traces.
samir: probe log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-21T23:02:14Z] tinyprobe eu1 p95=1203ms
[2026-03-21T23:03:11Z] tinyprobe eu1 p95=1189ms
[2026-03-21T23:04:05Z] tinyprobe eu1 p95=605ms
```
maya: Thanks — looks like it correlates with a short GC on one GPU host. Host ID gpunode-09 had a 21:03 kernel oom-kill? but recovered.
tj: If it's single-host and transient, no rollback needed. Recommend: pin traffic away from gpunode-09 for 10m and re-run probe set. @oncall can you carve a maintenance pin?
oncall: Pin created: traffic-weight(eu1, gpunode-09) -> 0 for 10m. Noted in runbook RC3-eu1.
samir: I've re-run the tinyprobe against the shardpool excluding gpunode-09, p95 stable ~420ms across 50 samples.
lina: Traces show increased kv-cache misses at ~21:02 on that host, plus a scheduler CPU steal spike. Likely background process bumped memory.
maya: Action items: 1) Keep pin for 10m and monitor; 2) run full smoke suite (tiny + semantic) in eu1 after pin removal; 3) ops to check host housekeeping jobs. If we see another p95 > 1s within 30m, escalate to rollback.
tj: Agreed. I'll set the smoke-run job now: ```./tools/run-smoke --env=eu1 --suite=tiny,semantic --samples=100```
deploy-bot: Smoke job queued as smoke-6975302500. Will post results when done.
ops-bot: Note added to incident log: small transient latency spike post-deploy, mitigated with host pin.
maya: Thanks all — I'll keep this thread updated. If smoke job returns clean we call this closed. :thumbsup:
